title: Soft 6
content:
Leaving Little Apple tied at the foot of the mountain, Wei Wuxian stepped over the crumbling remains of the stone barrier and headed up the path. Before long, he came upon a headless stone beast. Weighing over a thousand catties, it had guarded this mountain trail for years, smothered in tangled vines and moss. Its head had been sheared clean off with a heavy axe and smashed to powder nearby in a petty display of spite, the fresh fracture gleaming chalky white. Further up, another guardian beast had been split straight down the middle from crest to base.

Wei Wuxian didn't need to guess: after his death, the prominent clans had planted these warding beasts directly over the Burial Mounds’ spiritual pressure points. Sculpted to suppress yin energy and repel malevolent wraiths, they required master craftsmanship and cost an absolute fortune. Seeing them trashed like common rubble was a crying waste of good stone.

He took a few steps alongside Lan Wangji, glancing back over his shoulder to find that Wen Ning had already caught up.

Wen Ning stood beside the broken beast, head bowed, utterly motionless. "Wen Ning? What are you looking at?"

Wen Ning pointed toward the plinth.

The stone beast sat propped on a thick, rounded tree stump. Clustered around it were three smaller, stubby stumps, charred black as coal by ancient fire.

Wen Ning dropped to his knees, his fingers digging deep into the dirt. Scooping up a handful of ash-dark earth, he curled his fingers tight around it, whispering, "...Jiejie."

Wei Wuxian didn't know what to say. He walked over, clapping a firm, heavy palm on his shoulder.

In his past life, two of his most agonizing chapters had played out on this mountain. He had never planned on making a nostalgic pilgrimage.

And for Wen Ning, the Burial Mounds was a place carved from pure nightmare.

A bone-chilling gust tore through the timber, setting the endless canopy hissing like tens of thousands of phantom whispers. Wei Wuxian tilted his ear, dropping to one knee. Leaning low, he breathed a barely audible murmur into the soil beneath his boots. Seconds later, the earth gave a tiny heave.

Like a pale blossom pushing through the blackened loam, a skeletal arm slowly broke the surface.

The fragile bone fingers curled and swayed in the air. Wei Wuxian reached out, gently closing his hand around the wrist. He leaned down even further, long dark hair tumbling over his shoulder to curtain half his face.

Pressing his lips near the bleached knuckles, he whispered a few soft syllables, then went still, listening to the ground. A beat later, he gave a faint nod. As if folding into a bud, the skeletal hand retracted, slipping soundlessly back beneath the soil.

Wei Wuxian pushed himself up, dusting off his robes. "Over the past few days, they’ve hauled more than a hundred captives up to the summit. All still breathing. But the ones who dragged them here have already cleared out. Whatever trap they're setting, watch your backs."

Pushing further uphill, dilapidated shacks began cropping up along the verge.

They were cramped, slapped together with crude timber, clearly thrown up in desperate haste. Some had been torched down to their charred frames; others leaned heavily on the verge of collapse. Even the best-preserved among them had an entire wall smashed to splinters. After thirteen years of weathering storms without a living soul to care for them, they stood like tattered, decaying phantoms, staring down in grim silence at the trespassers below.

Wen Ning’s stride had grown leaden from the moment they crossed the perimeter, and now, frozen before a crooked shack, his boots refused to budge.

It was a home he had built with his own hands. When he left, it had been whole. Humble, yes, but sturdy enough to keep the rain off the people he knew, the people he loved.

They often spoke of "the place remaining while the people fade"—at least there, the place remained. Here, there wasn't even enough left to mourn.

Wei Wuxian murmured, "Don't look."

Wen Ning choked out, "...I knew it would be like this. I just... wanted to see if anything was left—"

The floorboards creaked. Out from the ruined shack stumbled a shambling silhouette.

The figure lurched into the thin daylight, its rotting, half-decayed face bared to the sun. Wei Wuxian clapped his hands sharply, but the walking corpse didn't even flinch, dragging its boots straight toward them. Wei Wuxian drifted back two paces with easy grace. "Bound by the Yin Tiger Tally."

Corpses that had already bent the knee to him couldn't be hijacked by the Tally; conversely, whatever was chained to the Tally wouldn't obey his commands either. Brutally simple rules: first come, first served.

Wen Ning closed the gap in a single stride, ripping its head off with a guttural roar. Instantly, low snarls echoed from every corner of the woods. Creeping out from the dark pines came forty or fifty walking corpses—men, women, old, and young. Most were remarkably fresh, clad in burial shrouds, clearly the stolen dead from recent raids across the territories. Lan Wangji summoned his guqin, striking a chord with a flick of his wrist; the sonic wave rippled outward, forcing the closing circle of corpses straight onto their knees. Wen Ning hoisted a massive male corpse overhead, hurling it dozens of feet into the brush, leaving it impaled on a jagged pine branch, thrashing uselessly. Wei Wuxian called out, "Don't waste time brawling—head straight for the summit!"

Heaven only knew how many corpses Jin Guangyao had whipped into a frenzy with the Tally over the last few days. Horde after horde threw themselves forward. The three pushed up the slope, hacking through waves of flesh, the density of the dead thickening the closer they got to the peak. High above the ancient pines, guqin notes pierced the heavens, scattering murder after murder of shrieking crows. It took nearly two grueling hours before they finally carved out a moment to catch their breath.

Slumping down onto a shattered warding beast, Wei Wuxian exhaled a long breath, chuckling self-deprecatingly. "I used to point this weapon at everyone else; now it's my turn on the receiving end. I finally get why everyone hated the Yin Tiger Tally so damn much. If I were in their shoes, I’d want to strangle the bastard who invented it too."

Lan Wangji stowed his instrument. Slipping a longsword from his sleeve, he offered it forward. "For defense."

Wei Wuxian glanced down. It was Suibian. After cutting that watermelon the other day, he’d tossed it aside, and Lan Wangji had quietly scooped it up. He drew the steel an inch, staring at the pristine, snow-white glare of the edge before smoothly clicking it back into its sheath with a wry grin. "Thanks." He hooked it casually to his sash, showing zero intention of drawing it. Catching Lan Wangji’s unblinking stare, Wei Wuxian scratched his nose. "It's been so many years since I used a blade, I'm completely out of practice." He let out a theatrical sigh. "Alright, truth is, this new vessel has pathetic spiritual reserves. Even with a high-grade masterwork, I can't unleash a fraction of its true power. So, I’ll be troubling Hanguang-jun to look after this delicate, defenseless maiden."

Lan Wangji just stared at him, deadpan.

The "defenseless maiden" caught his breath for a beat, then hauled himself up by his knees. Continuing up the final stretch of the trail, a yawning, pitch-black maw finally materialized at the path's dead end.

The entrance gaped over fifty feet wide and tall. Long before they reached the threshold, a blast of icy yin wind rolled outward, laced with the faint, muffled hum of groaning voices.

The legendary epicenter of atrocities where the Yiling Laozu forged corpses and slaughtered the innocent—the Demon-Subduing Cave.

The cavern vaulted high overhead. Muffling their breath, the three ghosted inside without making a sound, the clamor of voices from the depths growing louder and more frantic with every step.

Knowing the layout like the back of his hand, Wei Wuxian took point, raising a flat palm to signal a halt.

A single stone partition separated them from the main cavern. Peering through a fissure in the rock face, they looked down upon an immense cavern capable of swallowing a thousand men. In the center sat over a hundred youths, their wrists and ankles bound tight by Deity-Binding Cords. Judging by their age, pristine robes, and spiritual blades, every single one was either an elite inner disciple or a direct clan heir.

Wei Wuxian traded a sharp glance with Lan Wangji. Before they could whisper a plan, a boy on the floor piped up: "If you ask me, you shouldn't have stopped at skewering his gut—you should've taken his head off!"

The cavern was an acoustic chamber; even a whisper bounced off the stalactites with ringing clarity. The voice carried an instantly recognizable rasp. It took Wei Wuxian a second to place it: wasn't that Jin Chan, the brat who’d tried to jump Jin Ling the other day?

Looking beside him, sitting sullen and dark-faced in the dirt, who else could it be but Jin Ling?

Jin Ling didn't even twitch, staring at the floor in stubborn silence. Beside him, another boy’s stomach gave an aggressive, audible rumble. "They dumped us here days ago—what the hell are they waiting for?! If they're gonna slit our throats, just get it over with! I'd rather get torn apart by a night-hunt beast than starve to death in the dirt!"

The endless complaining was undeniably Lan Jingyi. Jin Chan sneered, "What else would he want? He's gonna do what he did to the Wen dogs back in the Sunshot Campaign—refine us into mindless fierce corpses, then throw us at our own families so they can't bring themselves to fight back! Forcing our parents to butcher their own flesh and blood!" He ground his teeth, spitting, "Despicable Wei dog! Pure, inhuman filth!"

Jin Ling’s voice sliced through the gloom, icy and sharp: "Shut your mouth."

Jin Chan blinked in disbelief. "You telling me to shut up? What's that supposed to mean?"

"What does it mean?" Jin Ling snapped. "Are you deaf, or just an idiot? It means stop flapping your gums!"

Having spent days tied up in the dark, Jin Chan’s fuse was non-existent. "Who the hell are you to tell me what to do?!"

"What's the point of running your mouth?!" Jin Ling snarled. "You think bitching is gonna snap the ropes?! You're giving me a headache."

"Why, you—!"

A calm, level-headed voice cut in: "We're trapped in a cave with hundreds of fierce corpses pacing the woods, ready to breach the doors at any second. Is this really the time to pick a fight?"

Lan Sizhui. The boy was always the voice of reason. Jin Chan barked, "He's the one picking fights! What, you're allowed to curse him out, but I'm not?! Who do you think you are, Jin Ling?! Just 'cause Lianfang-zun is Chief Cultivator doesn't mean you're getting the throne next! I'm not shutting up—let's see you try and—"

Thud!

Jin Ling slammed his forehead straight into Jin Chan’s nose. Jin Chan let out an agonized howl, snarling, "You wanna go?! Let's go! I've been waiting for an excuse, you motherless bastard!"

Hearing that slur, Jin Ling saw red. With his hands bound tight, he weaponized his knees and elbows, driving brutal blows into the boy until Jin Chan shrieked in pain. But Jin Ling was alone, while Jin Chan was used to running with a pack; seeing their ringleader taking a beating, several disciples yelled, "I've got your back!" and swarmed him. Trapped in the splash zone, Lan Sizhui tried to play peacemaker, pleading, "Calm down, everyone, calm down!" But after catching two stray elbows to the ribs, his brow twitched, his face darkening until he snapped, letting out a frustrated yell and throwing himself into the brawl.

Watching the royal rumble from the shadows, the three adults had seen enough. Wei Wuxian bounded onto the stone stairs of the Demon-Subduing Cave, bellowing: "Hey! Eyes up here!"

The roar echoed through the subterranean chamber like a rolling thunderclap. The tangle of brawling teenagers froze, looking up in shock. Lan Sizhui caught sight of the white-robed silhouette beside him, his face lighting up: "Hanguang-jun!"

Lan Jingyi took it up an octave: "Hanguang-jun, save us!"

Jin Chan blanched in pure terror. "What are you cheering for?! They... they're working together!"

Wei Wuxian strode down the steps, smoothly drawing Suibian and tossing it over his shoulder. A dark blur caught the hilt midair—Wen Ning. The cavern dissolved into frantic, shrieking hysterics: "G-Ghost General!"

Wen Ning swung Suibian down toward Jin Ling. Jin Ling squeezed his eyes shut, bracing for the worst—only to feel the tight cords around his chest snap clean. Turning on his heel, Wen Ning drifted through the hall, slicing through the Deity-Binding Cords one by one. The freed disciples were caught in a paralyzing deadlock: flee or stay? Inside stood the Yiling Laozu, the Ghost General, and the disgraced Hanguang-jun; outside prowled hundreds of ravenous walking corpses. Trapped between a rock and a hard place, they shrank into the cavern corners, unblinking eyes tracking Wen Ning’s emotionless patrol.

Lan Sizhui, however, beamed with absolute relief. "Mo... Senior Wei. You came to save us, didn't you? You weren't the one who had us taken, right?"

Though framed as a question, his eyes radiated unconditional trust. A warm swell brushed Wei Wuxian’s ribs. Crouching down, he reached out and aggressively ruffled the boy’s hair, thoroughly mussing up the immaculate style Sizhui had maintained despite days in captivity. "Me? You know how broke I am—where would I find the silver to hire mercenaries?"

Sizhui nodded vigorously. "Right! I knew it! I know Senior is genuinely dirt-poor!"

Wei Wuxian's eyebrow twitched for a beat.

"Good boy," Wei Wuxian cleared his throat. "How many were there? Any ambushes stationed outside?"

Lan Jingyi kicked the frayed cords off his boots, rushing to cut in: "There were a ton of them! Their faces were masked by dark smoke so we couldn't make out a thing! They dumped us here and vanished, like they wanted us to rot! Oh, and the woods outside are crawling with corpses! Screaming non-stop!"

Bichen cleared its scabbard with a crystalline chime, slicing the remaining cords from the disciples. Sheathing the blade, Lan Wangji looked down at Lan Sizhui. "Well done."

A quiet commendation for keeping his head, and for keeping his faith. Sizhui scrambled to his feet, straightening his spine before his senior with disciplined poise. Before a smile could break across his face, Wei Wuxian teased, "Truly well done, Sizhui. Look at you, learning how to brawl like a champion."

Sizhui’s cheeks flared a bright, mortified crimson. "T-that was... a momentary lapse of reason..."

A shift in the air caught Wei Wuxian’s attention. Turning around, he found Jin Ling standing stiffly behind them.

Lan Wangji stepped cleanly in front of Wei Wuxian, while Lan Sizhui immediately stepped in front of Lan Wangji, offering a cautious, "Young Master Jin."

Wei Wuxian peeked out from behind the wall of white robes, amused. "What are you two playing at? Stacking up like a human tower?"

Jin Ling’s face was a tempest of tangled emotions. His fists clenched, loosened, and clenched again, words catching in his throat as his eyes remained glued to the fresh scar on Wei Wuxian’s abdomen—the exact spot he had run through with his sword.

Lan Jingyi gasped in horror, "You... you aren't thinking of stabbing him again, are you?!"

Jin Ling’s expression went rigid. Sizhui warned, "Jingyi!"

Wei Wuxian hooked an arm around Jingyi's neck with his left hand and Sizhui's with his right, steering both boys toward the entrance. "Alright, wrap it up. Everyone outside, now."

Sizhui nodded instantly. "Yes, sir!"

The disciples huddled in the corners remained paralyzed with fear. Lan Jingyi barked, "Move it! You planning on setting up camp here?!"

One boy lifted his chin defensively. "The woods are swarming with corpses! You want us to walk out there and die?!"

Wen Ning spoke up quietly: "Gongzi, I will go clear a path."

Wei Wuxian nodded, and Wen Ning shot out of the cave like a gust of dark wind. Sizhui called out to the stragglers, "Our hands are free! Worst-case scenario, we fight our way through together! If you stay behind and the horde breaches the cave once we leave, this cavern will become your tomb!"

Grabbing Jingyi by the sleeve, he led the Lan juniors out behind Wen Ning. The remaining disciples exchanged wide-eyed, panicked stares.

A beat later, someone shouted, "Sizhui-xiong, wait for me!" and sprinted after them.

It was Ouyang Zizhen, the romantic boy who had shed tears and burned paper money for A-Qing back in Yi City. Seeing him break rank, several familiar faces from Yi City fell into step. The rest of the disciples hesitated, but catching the unblinking stares of Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji—both equally terrifying in their own right—they gritted their teeth and scurried past.

Bringing up the rear was Jin Ling.

Just as the crowd shuffled toward the daylight of the cave mouth, a silhouette came hurtling backward through the air, slamming violently into the cavern wall with a concussive crack!

Stone dust showered the floor. Up ahead, several disciples shrieked in horror: "The Ghost General!"

Wei Wuxian stepped forward. "Wen Ning? What happened?!"

Wen Ning’s voice was strained: "...I'm fine."

Tumbling out of the crater in the rock, he stood up and bluntly shoved his dislocated arm back into its socket with a sickening pop. Wei Wuxian looked past him toward the entrance, his eyes narrowing.

Standing at the threshold of the Demon-Subduing Cave was a young man draped in sweeping violet silks, Zidian crackling with arcs of vicious purple lightning around his knuckles.

It had been that whip strike that blasted Wen Ning clean through the cavern.

Jiang Cheng.

No wonder Wen Ning hadn't raised a hand to defend himself.

Jin Ling called out, "Jiujiu!"

Jiang Cheng’s voice was arctic: "Jin Ling. Over here."

Emerging from the black pines behind him came an endless tide of cultivators draped in the colorful crests of the prominent sects. The ranks swelled by the second—nearly two thousand strong—encircling the mouth of the Demon-Subduing Cave in an iron ring. Every man among them, Jiang Cheng included, was soaked in fresh gore, looking thoroughly battered from forced marches. Seeing their families, the rescued heirs bolted from the cave with tearful shouts: "Father!" "Mother!" "Brother!" throwing themselves into the ranks.

Jin Ling looked between the two sides, his boots frozen on the threshold. Jiang Cheng barked, "What are you stalling for, Jin Ling?! Get over here right now! Are you asking to die?!"

Standing at the vanguard of the allied force was Lan Qiren. He looked noticeably aged, silver creeping heavily through the hair at his temples. He called out softly, "Wangji."

Lan Wangji lowered his chin. "Uncle."

Yet he didn't budge an inch toward the righteous ranks.

The refusal was absolute. A look of devastating disappointment washed across Lan Qiren’s face; he closed his eyes, shaking his head, offering no further lecture.

A maiden draped in flowing white stepped out from the formation, tears shimmering in her lashes. "Hanguang-jun, what has become of you? You... you are no longer the man you were. You were once his bitterest rival, sworn opposites beneath the heavens. What sorcery did the Yiling Laozu wield to poison your mind, to force you onto the wrong side of righteousness?!"

Lan Wangji offered her not a single glance. Rebuffed by stone-cold silence, she could only let out a mournful sigh: "To think a paragon of virtue could fall this low... A crying waste of a noble name!"

Wei Wuxian drawled, "Here you all are again."

Jiang Cheng sneered, "Naturally."

Carrying his seven-stringed guqin across his back, Su She stepped to the front, drawling with oily composure, "Had the Yiling Laozu not returned to the living world with such desperate fanfare—desecrating graves and kidnapping heirs—I doubt we would have been compelled to visit your wretched den so soon."

Wei Wuxian arched a brow. "I literally just saved your heirs, yet you bypass the gratitude and jump straight to the indictment?"

Derisive snorts rippled through the ranks, accompanied by sneers of 'the thief crying thief.' Knowing petty bickering was entirely pointless, Wei Wuxian offered a thin, amused smirk. "Though, your vanguard looks a little threadbare today. You're missing two rather prominent figures. Might I ask where Lianfang-zun and Ze-wu-jun have run off to during such an auspicious gathering?"

Su She scoffed coldly, "Lianfang-zun was gravely wounded by an assassin's blade at Koi Tower just two days ago; Ze-wu-jun is currently pouring all his strength into saving his life. Why play dumb when you orchestrated the hit yourself?"

Hearing that Jin Guangyao was "gravely wounded," the image of him running himself through with a sword back in the day flashed through Wei Wuxian’s mind. Unable to hold it back, he snorted, letting out an audible burst of laughter.

Su She’s brow twitched. "What are you laughing at?"

"Nothing," Wei Wuxian chuckled. "Just amused by how often Lianfang-zun finds himself wounded."

From the crowd, a timid voice piped up: "Father, I really don't think he did it. He saved us back in Yi City, and it felt like he came to rescue us just now too..."

Wei Wuxian glanced over; it was Ouyang Zizhen again. But his father barked him down instantly: "Mind your tongue, boy! Do you have any idea what kind of assembly this is?! Do you have any idea what kind of monster you're defending?!"

Wei Wuxian pulled his gaze back, murmuring calmly, "I see."

He had known from the start that no one would believe a word he said. What he denied would be forced onto him; what he admitted would be twisted into atrocities.

Lan Wangji’s reputation had once carried immense weight, but by standing at his side, he had painted a target across his own back. He had hoped Lan Xichen would be present to mediate, but neither the Chief Cultivator nor Ze-wu-jun had shown their faces.

Thirteen years ago, during the first siege of the Burial Mounds, Jin Guangshan commanded the Lanling Jin, and Jiang Cheng led the Yunmeng Jiang. Lan Qiren steered Gusu Lan, and Nie Mingjue spearheaded Qinghe Nie. The first two were the bloodthirsty vanguard; the latter two were merely fulfilling political obligations. Today, the Jin clan leader was absent, delegating his forces to the Lan Clan's command; Gusu was once again steered by Lan Qiren; and Nie Huaisang had inherited his brother's seat, shrinking behind the mob with his signature 'I know nothing, I want no part of this, I'm just here to fill the headcount' expression plastered across his face.

Only Jiang Cheng remained unchanged: radiating pure, unadulterated venom, his murderous glare locked dead onto Wei Wuxian's face.

And yet.

Wei Wuxian turned his head slightly.

Standing right beside him—devoid of hesitation, devoid of fear—was Lan Wangji.

This time, he wasn't standing alone.

Amidst the sea of drawn blades, a middle-aged cultivator’s patience broke. Leaping forward, he barked, "Wei Wuxian! Do you remember me?!"

Wei Wuxian answered with complete honesty: "Not in the slightest."

The man sneered with bitter satisfaction. "You don't remember, but my leg remembers!"

He hoisted his robe, revealing a carved wooden peg leg. "You shattered this limb that night in Nightless City! I show you this so you know that when you fall today, Yi Weichun had a hand in putting you in the dirt! The heavens have eyes—karma always collects its debt!"

Bolstered by his speech, a young cultivator strode out from the ranks, his voice ringing loud: "Wei Wuxian, I won't bother asking if you remember me! My parents both fell to your sorcery; you drown in so much blood you couldn't possibly recall two elderly souls! But I, Fang Mengchen, will never forget! And I will never forgive!"

A third man stepped forward—tall, gaunt, carrying the dignified air of an upright scholar. Wei Wuxian beat him to the punch, asking casually, "Did I cripple you too?"

The scholar shook his head.

"Did I murder your parents, or wipe out your clan?"

He shook his head again.

Wei Wuxian blinked, amused. "Then what are you doing here?"

The scholar declared, "I hold no personal grudge against you! I came today to make one thing clear: a fiend who defies all under heaven deserves nothing less than death! No matter what foul sorcery you practice, no matter how many times you crawl out of your grave, we will send you right back down to hell! Not for vengeance—but for justice!"

A thunderous cheer erupted from the crowd: "Well spoken, Sect Leader Yao!"

Sect Leader Yao bowed with a self-satisfied smirk, stepping back as the crowd’s bloodlust caught fire. One by one, voices rose to declare their righteous crusades:

"My son took a blade through the throat from your dog Wen Ning at Qiongqi Path!"

"My martial brother rotted alive from your vile blood curse!"

"We stand here today to prove that righteousness still reigns, and evil will find no mercy!"

"Righteousness still reigns! Evil finds no mercy!"

Every face was flushed with righteous fervor; every word dripped with moral supremacy. Each man stood tall, bathed in heroic indignation and boundless glory.

Not a single soul among them harbored the slightest doubt: what they were doing today was a glorious crusade, a magnificent triumph for the ages.

A crusade of "good" putting down "evil," destined to be carved into history for ten thousand generations to praise!
